segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then I looked, and there was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion, and with him one hundred forty-four thousand who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I heard a sound from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder, and the sound I heard was like harpists playing on their harps.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they sing something like a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders, and no one could learn the song except the one hundred forty-four thousand, who had been bought from the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: These are the ones who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were bought from among humankind as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and in their mouth no lie was found; they are without blemish.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then I saw another angel flying high overhead, with eternal good news to announce to those who live on the earth, to every nation and tribe and language and people,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying in a loud voice,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Fear God and give him glory, because the hour of his judgment has come. Worship the one who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of water.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And another angel, a second, followed, saying,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And another angel, a third, followed them, saying in a loud voice,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives a mark on the forehead or on the hand,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: that person too will drink the wine of God’s fury, poured undiluted into the cup of his wrath, and will be tormented with fire and sulfur before holy angels and before the Lamb.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And the smoke of their torment rises forever and ever, and they have no rest day or night, those who worship the beast and its image, and anyone who receives the mark of its name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This calls for the endurance of the holy ones, those who keep the commandments of God and their faith in Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I heard a voice from heaven saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.”

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yes,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: says the Spirit,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “so that they may rest from their labors, for their deeds follow along with them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was one like a son of man, with a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And another angel came out of the sanctuary, crying out in a loud voice to the one seated on the cloud,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Put in your sickle and reap, because the hour to reap has come, for the harvest of the earth is ripe.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the one seated on the cloud swung his sickle over the earth, and the earth was reaped.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then another angel came out of the sanctuary in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And another angel, the one who has authority over the fire, came out from the altar, and he called in a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Put in your sharp sickle and gather the clusters from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are fully ripe.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the clusters from the vine of the earth, and threw them into the great winepress of God’s fury.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood flowed from the winepress as high as the horses’ bridles for a distance of one thousand six hundred stadia.

notes.note: The verb is the ordinary word for buying in a market, the same one used for buying and selling in 13:17. Most translations have “redeemed” here, though some have “purchased.” The image is of a purchase that transfers ownership to God, as in 5:9, and “redeemed” belongs more properly to a different Greek word group.

Taken literally, this describes a company of celibate men. Most interpreters read it figuratively: Israel’s soldiers abstained from sex while on campaign, and the prophets describe idolatry as sexual unfaithfulness, so the picture is of a people who have kept themselves from the worship of the beast. Which reading is intended remains disputed.

In the Septuagint this is the regular term for a sacrificial animal free of any defect. Coming directly after “firstfruits,” another offering term, the sacrificial sense is probably intended. Most translations have “blameless,” which the word can also mean when used of moral character.

The Greek word was an ordinary term for a public announcement of good news, and “gospel” now sounds like a religious term or a book title. The Greek here has no article, and the announcement that follows is a summons to fear and worship the Creator because his judgment has arrived. Many modern translations alternate between “gospel” and “good news.”

This is the same Greek word that this translation renders “Gentiles” where it refers to the non-Jewish peoples. In Revelation’s lists of nation, tribe, language and people, and in “all the nations” in verse 8, the peoples of the whole world are meant, so “nation” is used.

The cry echoes Isaiah 21:9. Babylon, the empire that destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in the sixth century BC, serves in Revelation as the name of a great oppressing city. Most scholars identify it with Rome.

The Greek word is the same one rendered “fury” in verses 10 and 19, and it can mean either intense passion or anger. Many translations take it as “passion” here; others render “wrath,” so that the wine Babylon serves the nations already carries God’s anger. The echo between Babylon’s wine and God’s wine in verse 10 is almost certainly deliberate. The sexual immorality is a prophetic figure for the idolatry and corrupting alliances into which the city draws the nations.

The Greek is literally “mixed unmixed.” Wine was normally diluted with water before drinking, and the verb for mixing had come to mean simply preparing or pouring wine, so the phrase means wine served at full strength. The cup of God’s wrath is an image from the prophets, for example Jeremiah 25:15.

“Saints” now suggests canonized individuals or people of exceptional virtue. The Greek word is used of all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Septuagint’s language for Israel. Many translations keep “saints”; others use “God’s people.”

The Greek is literally “the faith of Jesus.” It can mean faith in Jesus, which most translations adopt, or Jesus’s own faithfulness, or the faith that comes from Jesus. The word “their” is supplied for the sake of English.

notes.phrase: one like a son of man
notes.traditional: one like unto the Son of man
notes.note: The phrase echoes Daniel 7:13, where a human-looking figure comes with the clouds of heaven; the same wording describes the risen Jesus in 1:13. Most interpreters identify the figure here as Christ. A minority take him to be an angel, because “another angel” follows and gives him the command to reap. The Greek lacks the article found in the Gospel title “the Son of Man,” so the phrase is left in lowercase.

Greek has two words that English Bibles usually both render “temple”: one for the whole complex with its courts, and this one for the building where God dwells. “Sanctuary” keeps the distinction; here it is the heavenly dwelling of God from which the angels come. Most translations use “temple” for both words.

notes.traditional: a thousand and six hundred furlongs
notes.note: A stadion was about 185 meters, so the distance is roughly 300 kilometers or 180 miles. The figure is kept rather than converted because it is probably symbolic: sixteen hundred is four squared times ten squared, and four is Revelation’s number for the whole earth. Some translations convert it to “two hundred miles.”

candidates.reason: Used of literal buying and of God’s acquisition of people (1 Cor 6:20; 7:23; 2 Pet 2:1; Rev 5:9; 14:3–4), where versions vary between “redeemed,” “purchased” and “bought” and blur it with λυτρόω.
Paired with ὀργή throughout Revelation and Paul; a fixed pair such as fury/wrath is needed so the two words stay distinct, and the “wine of the θυμός of her πορνεία” formula recurs in 18:3.

Recurs across the Gospels, Paul and Revelation with renderings ranging from “fornication” to “sexual immorality” to “prostitution,” and Revelation’s link with πόρνη (the prostitute Babylon) needs a consistent decision.
Frequent across the New Testament and rendered variously as “patience,” “perseverance,” “steadfastness” and “endurance”; the formula “Here is the endurance of the holy ones” also recurs in 13:10.
Occurs in the Gospels, 1 Corinthians and Revelation; a policy is needed on keeping the ancient unit versus converting to miles, especially where the number may be symbolic.
